issues.legal_issue: An accused cannot claim a right of private defence of property to justify an assault when the land was in the exclusive possession of the persons obstructing the accused’s attempt to occupy it.
material_facts: The courts below concurrently found that the land where the accused sought to stack their crop bundles was in the exclusive possession of the deceased’s party.
The accused sought to place the bundles on that land, and the deceased objected before the accused assaulted him and his brother.
issues.conclusion: The accused had no right of private defence of property, and the claim was rejected.
issues.legal_principle: The asserted right of private defence of property did not apply because the land was found to be in the exclusive possession of the persons who resisted the accused’s attempted occupation. The court relied on no earlier cases or specific statutory provision in deciding this point.

rule.if: criminal_appeal and land_exclusively_possessed_by_obstructors and accused_attempted_forcible_occupation and obstructors_resisted_occupation

predicates.criminal_appeal: The case is a criminal appeal challenging the accused’s convictions.
predicates.land_exclusively_possessed_by_obstructor: The land at the scene was found to be in the exclusive possession of the persons who resisted the accused.
predicates.accused_attempted_forcible_occupation: The accused attempted to occupy or use the land against the wishes of those in possession.
predicates.obstructors_resisted_occupation: The persons in possession objected to the accused’s attempted occupation or use of the land.
predicates.private_defence_of_property_unavailable: The accused cannot rely on a right of private defence of property to justify the assault.

issues.definition: When, in a criminal appeal, the obstructors exclusively possess the land and resist the accused’s forcible attempt to occupy it, the accused cannot rely on private defence of property.

issues.legal_issue: Common intention to cause death is not established for every participant in a group assault merely because the participants acted together, but may be established for participants who jointly inflict fatal injuries in circumstances showing a shared intention to cause those injuries.
material_facts: Two accused, each armed with a stick, each struck the deceased forcefully on the head, causing one injury apiece; the resulting head injuries were sufficient in the ordinary course of nature to cause death.
The other two accused assaulted the deceased and his brother with kicks and fists.

The court found no evidence that all four had arrived with a preplanned intention to cause the deceased’s death, and held that the other two’s participation and the armed assailants’ use of sticks did not establish their shared intention to cause death.
The appeal challenged convictions for murder with the aid of the common-intention provision.
issues.conclusion: The murder convictions of the two accused who each delivered a forceful blow to the deceased’s head were maintained because they developed and shared the intention to cause the fatal injuries when delivering the blows. The murder convictions of the other two accused were set aside because the evidence did not establish their common intention to cause death.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 302 and 34 of the Penal Code, common intention to cause the relevant fatal injury must be established; knowledge that weapons would be used in an assault is not, by itself, enough to establish a common intention to commit murder. Common intention may arise at the time of the occurrence, and the court inferred it for the two assailants who each delivered a forceful head blow sufficient in the ordinary course of nature to cause death. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: criminal_appeal and ((each_of_two_assailants_delivered_forceful_head_blow and head_injuries_sufficient_to_cause_death) or (other_participants_used_only_nonfatal_assault and no_evidence_of_shared_intention_to_cause_death))

predicates.criminal_appeal: The case is a criminal appeal challenging convictions for murder attributed to a group acting with a shared intention.
predicates.each_of_two_assailants_delivered_forcefu: Each of two assailants forcefully struck the victim on the head.
predicates.head_injuries_sufficient_to_cause_death: The injuries caused by the head blows were sufficient in the ordinary course of nature to cause death.
predicates.other_participants_used_only_nonfatal_as: The other participants assaulted the victim without delivering the fatal head blows.
predicates.no_evidence_of_shared_intention_to_cause: The evidence did not show that the other participants shared an intention to cause death.
predicates.murder_conviction_under_common_intention: The murder conviction is maintained for the assailants who jointly inflicted fatal injuries and set aside for the other participants whose shared intention to cause death was not established.

issues.definition: When, in a criminal appeal, two assailants each deliver a forceful head blow sufficient to cause death, their murder convictions are maintained; when the other participants use only nonfatal force and evidence of their shared intention to cause death is absent, their murder convictions are set aside.
